 Judgment

This appeal has been filed by the claimant in OP(MV) No.960 of 2009 on the files of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ottapalam, a claim petition filed under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short, "the Act").
The respondents herein were the respondents before the tribunal.

2. The case of the claimant is that on 30.03.2006, while he was travelling in an autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KL-50V TN 39 U- 6136 from Annur to Thiruppur, the autorickshaw hit on the rearside of a lorry bearing Reg.No.KL-TDH 6109, which was parked on the road side in a negligent manner, whereby he sustained serious injuries.
He approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 2,00,000/-.

3. Respondents 1 and 2, who are the driver and owner of the offending vehicle respectively,
remained ex parte before the tribunal.

The third respondent insurer filed a written statement,
admitting the policy coverage for the offending vehicle, but disputing the liability and quantum of compensation claimed.
PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A9 & B1 to B4 were marked.

The tribunal,
after 2025:KER:86881 ..3..
analysing the pleadings and materials on record, dismissed the claim petition for non-jointer of necessary parties.
Challenging the dismissal of the claim petition, the claimant has come up in appeal.
4. I have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent insurer.
Since the policy is admitted and no right of recovery is ordered against respondents 1 and 2, who are the driver and owner of the offending lorry, notice to them is dispensed with.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant submits that the claim was put forward against the driver,
owner and the insurer of the offending lorry, however, the tribunal dismissed the claim petition,
finding that since the charge sheet was drawn against the driver of the autorickshaw, the appellant is not entitled to get any compensation from the insurer of the lorry.
It is further submitted that the claim petition being filed under Section 163A of the Act, the appellant is entitled to compensation.
I find force in the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant.

When a claim petition is filed under Section 163A of the Act, the tribunal, for awarding compensation, need not look into the aspect of negligence as held by the Full Bench of this Court in Suresh v. Vasantha Shetty [2025 (5)
KHC 520].

Accordingly, I hold that the 2025:KER:86881 ..4..
appellant is entitled to get compensation as is specified under the second schedule to Section 163A of the Act.
6.

The learned counsel for the appellant claims compensation under the following heads:

sentences.text: Permanent disability -
The learned counsel for the appellant submits that in the claim petition, for assessing compensation, the appellant claimed a monthly income of 3,000/- as a salesman in a bakery.
The appellant was aged 24 years at the time of the accident and as per Ext.A6 disability certificate, he sustained 15% disability.

Since the claim petition was filed under Section 163A of the Act and the appellant claimed only an amount of 3,000/- as the monthly income, I deem it appropriate to fix the annual income of the appellant at 36,000/- for assessing compensation towards permanent disability.
The multiplier to be adopted as per the schedule to Section 163A of the Act is '17'.
Thus, the appellant will be entitled to get a compensation of 91,800/- (36000 x 17 x 15%) for permanent disability.
6.2. Loss of earnings -
The learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant was a salesman in a bakery and due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he could not go to work for a period of six months.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained and 2025:KER:86881 ..5..
the age of the appellant, I am of the opinion that four months can be taken for awarding compensation for loss of earnings.
Accordingly, the appellant is awarded a total compensation of 12,000/- (3000 x 4) under this head.
6.3. Pain and suffering -
Considering the injuries sustained by him and the sufferings that he had undergone, I am inclined to grant an amount of 5,000/- to the appellant as compensation towards pain and suffering.
Thus, the appellant will be entitled to get an amount of 5,000/- as compensation towards pain and suffering.
6.4. Medical expenses - The learned counsel for the appellant submits that as per Ext.A9 medical bills, the appellant spent an amount of 37,000/- towards medical bills.

As per the schedule to Section 163A of the Act, the maximum amount that can be awarded towards medical expenses is 15,000/- and accordingly, I award a compensation of 15,000/- towards medical expenses.
7. Since the appeal is of the year 2013, I fix interest on the enhanced compensation @ 7% per annum from the date of the claim petition till realization.

Thus, the impugned award of the tribunal is modified as follows:

Medical expenses 15000

Total 1,23,800 Ravi@ Ravindrakumar vs Kamaraj on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141261589/
3

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part and the appellant is awarded a total compensation of 1,23,800/- (Rupees one lakh twenty three thousand and eight hundred only) with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of petition till realization and proportionate costs.
The respondent insurer shall deposit the said amount together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The appellant shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, AADHAAR Card and bank details before the respondent insurer within a period of one month so as to enable the insurance company to make the deposit as ordered above.
In case of failure to furnish details as above, it shall be open for the insurance company to deposit the said amount before the tribunal.
Upon such deposit being made, the entire amount shall be disbursed to the appellant at the earliest in accordance with law.
